title: Genital herpes: symptoms, treatment and protecting partners
intro: Genital herpes is caused by herpes simplex viruses. Painful blisters or ulcers may recur, but many infections are unnoticed. A diagnosis cannot establish when infection occurred or prove recent infidelity.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Skin contact during vaginal, anal or oral sex can transmit the virus when sores are absent. Tingling may precede an outbreak; other conditions can also cause genital sores.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: Seek sexual-health assessment while a fresh lesion can be swabbed. Discuss other infection tests and pregnancy; routine blood testing is not always useful for explaining a particular sore. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Oral antivirals can shorten outbreaks; suppressive treatment may help frequent recurrences and reduce transmission. They do not remove the virus; topical cold-sore creams are not an adequate substitute. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Avoid sexual contact with the affected area from warning symptoms until healing. Condoms reduce but do not eliminate transmission. Gentle washing, loose clothing and individualized pain relief may improve comfort. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Difficulty passing urine, severe illness or eye symptoms need prompt care. Contact maternity care for a first suspected outbreak during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy; delivery planning is individualized.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira notices tingling before recurrent sores. She follows her early-treatment plan and pauses sexual contact without waiting for visible blisters.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben discusses prevention with a partner. They understand symptom-free periods and condom use do not guarantee zero risk.
